items.summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
items.title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

items.summary: Full-duplex speech models require training data that preserves turn-taking, overlap, interruption, and backchannel behavior, yet these signals are entangled across speakers in noisy real-world recordings. We present Conversational Voice, a pipeline that converts real two-speaker excerpts into three complementary training-data artifacts. (1) Separation recovers speaker-specific tracks with stable speaker assignments, a canonical transcript, and naturally observed interaction timing. (2) Reconstruction generates speech in matched voices from a fixed source transcript, reconstructs the source turn order, pauses, and overlaps, and adds word-level alignment and delivery instructions. (3) Expansion generates new dialogue constrained by the source context, speakers, and observed interaction pattern. Automatic speaker-verification metrics remain strong across stages, with same-speaker similarity of 0.983-0.991 and positive discrimination margins of 0.199-0.209. Predicted speech quality (NISQA MOS) is 3.56 for separation, 4.41 for reconstruction, and 4.61 for expansion. A Gemini-based automatic evaluator assigns expansion mean scores of 4.94/5 for contextual coherence and 4.80/5 for dialogue naturalness. Expansion and reconstruction exhibit broadly similar interaction profiles; expansion's turn, overlap-event, backchannel, and interruption rates are 4.6%, 8.0%, 13.2%, and 16.0% lower, respectively. We evaluate data properties only; downstream gains in full-duplex model training remain for future work.
items.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion

items.summary: We develop a rigorous reduction inside the Connes–Consani–Moscovici programme for the Riemann hypothesis. The main unconditional result is the following symmetry principle: for the truncated Weil quadratic form QW_λ^N, simplicity of the lowest eigenvalue ε_N implies evenness of the corresponding ground state ξ, provided the natural reflection symmetry γV_n = V_{-n} and the normalization ℓ_N(ξ) = 1 are imposed. This converts two structural requirements of the programme into one spectral requirement. We then prove a precise spectral approximation criterion. If the finite-dimensional form QW_λ^N approximates the prolate wave operator PW_λ in a form-strong sense sufficient to preserve the first isolated simple eigenvalue, then ε_N is simple for all large N. Combining this criterion with the symmetry principle gives evenness of the ground state. Finally, we prove a windowed determinant criterion for the Riemann hypothesis. If the regularized determinants attached to the Connes–Consani–Moscovici finite-rank perturbations have only real zeros and converge locally uniformly, on an exhausting family of windows, to nonzero multiples of the Riemann Ξ-function, then every zero of Ξ is real, and therefore the Riemann hypothesis follows. The paper separates cleanly the proved logical reductions from the analytic objectives required for their unconditional verification. Those objectives are collected in a final section of open problems, giving a foundational reference for the remaining work in the programme. We emphasize that this paper does not claim an unconditional proof of the Riemann hypothesis; rather, it provides a precise structural reduction and isolates the remaining analytic challenges.
items.title: Evenness from Simplicity in the Truncated Weil Quadratic Form and Conditional Spectral Criteria for the Riemann Hypothesis

items.summary: The spoof speech detection (SSD) is the essential countermeasure for automatic speaker verification systems. Although SSD with magnitude features in the frequency domain has shown promising results, the phase information also can be important to capture the artefacts of certain types of spoofing attacks. Thus, both magnitude and phase features must be considered to ensure the generalization ability to diverse types of spoofing attacks. In this paper, we investigate the failure reason of feature-level fusion of the previous works through the entropy analysis from which we found that the randomness difference between magnitude and phase features is large, which can interrupt the feature-level fusion via backend neural network; thus, we propose a phase network to reduce that difference. Our SSD system: phase network equipped Res2Net achieved significant performance improvement, specifically in the spoofing attack for which the phase information is considered to be important. Also, we demonstrate our SSD system in both known- and unknown-kind SSD scenarios for practical applications.
items.title: Phase-Aware Spoof Speech Detection Based on Res2Net with Phase Network

items.summary: Four-dimensional beam-matrix reconstruction from quadrupole scans is the standard way to mea- sure cross-plane coupling and the intrinsic emittances that a decoupling section can recover. We show that a scan of a single thin quadrupole, normal or skew and placed anywhere in a linear lattice, determines at most nine of the ten beam-matrix parameters for any number of settings, because each measured second moment is quadratic in the quadrupole strength. The unmeasured direction lies in the x–y cross block and has a closed form in terms of the transfer matrices; for a quadrupole followed by a drift of length L its nonzero entries are Wxpy = Wpxy = 1 and Wpxpy = −2/L. Both projected emittances are therefore measured, but the beam matrices consistent with the data form a line segment along which the smaller intrinsic emittance ranges from zero to slightly above its true value, so a single-knob scan gives only an upper bound on it. A thick quadrupole restores the miss- ing direction only weakly, its singular value scaling approximately as the sixth power of the magnet length. Scanning two independently powered quadrupoles of any type makes the reconstruction well posed without additional hardware.
items.title: Single-knob quadrupole scans do not determine the intrinsic emittances

items.summary: Replication files for “Bans versus Controlled Access: Reserve Substitution and Issuer Buybacks under Financial Sanctions”. The A7A5 archive covers the TRON base contract TLeVfrdym8RoJreJ23dAGyfJDygRtiWKBZ from 7–27 August 2025 UTC. Data were retrieved on 17 October 2026 UTC. It includes 5,244 unique events from 37 daily response pages, additional event-class and receipt checks, frozen source responses and request provenance, event-level records, daily and weekly aggregates, supply accounting, data definitions, and analysis and verification scripts. Coverage is specific to the queried contract and provider. Gross transfers do not measure trading volume, beneficial ownership, reserve flows, or issuer buyback expenditure. The pilot is descriptive and does not identify a causal sanctions effect. The model archive contains Python scripts and supplied outputs for hypothetical numerical examples of route substitution, constrained issuer purchases, monitoring-dependent depth, surplus access and fallback. Parameters are not calibrated to A7A5. Both archives use Python 3.9 or later and its standard library; their README files give offline reproduction commands. Access: metadata are public; files are restricted and available on request to the corresponding author, hyoungkang@hanyang.ac.kr. The accompanying RIGHTS_AND_SOURCES.md distinguishes author-created materials from third-party responses. Rights in original materials are reserved; no blanket open license is granted for the mixed archive. The associated manuscript is unpublished.
items.title: A7A5 pilot data and model replication files for Bans versus Controlled Access

items.summary: Embedding enhancement improves speaker verification under acoustic mismatch without modifying a frozen backbone. Recent work has established a practical label-free setting for this task, but often adopts increasingly structured formulations. Here, the clean target is directly observed during training, making enhancement a matching problem on the unit hypersphere. We model the clean target with a von Mises--Fisher (vMF) likelihood and profile out a sample-wise concentration parameter, yielding a simple closed-form objective with adaptive weighting. Across VoxCeleb1, VoxSRC23, CN-Celeb, VOiCES, and VC-Mix, the proposed method largely preserves the baseline and gives clearer gains on challenging mismatch sets. It also remains stable under a broad single-view recipe, where a recent diffusion baseline becomes less reliable in controlled comparisons. These results suggest that effective label-free embedding enhancement in this setting does not require a highly structured formulation.
items.title: Revisiting Label-Free Speaker Embedding Enhancement with vMF Profile Likelihood

items.summary: We present DECAF, a privacy preserving neural speech codec that obfuscates a speaker's voice while preserving linguistic content while maintaining automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance at very low bitrates, inspired by decaffeination. At the transmitter end, speech is encoded into speaker independent content embeddings, which are compressed using residual vector quantization and transmitted without any speaker related information. At the receiver, a canonical speaker embedding, shared a priori between endpoints, is used for waveform reconstruction, enabling deterministic and consistent obfuscation of a speaker's voice. The proposed framework leverages an information bottleneck applied to self supervised representations, along with a separate speaker embedding branch, to achieve effective speaker content disentanglement. We further incorporate a CTC-based auxiliary objective, encouraging content representations that are well aligned with downstream ASR tasks. We show that DECAF operating at a bit rate of 0.5 kbps achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of up to 43.5% for a speaker verification system, while maintaining competitive ASR performance, yielding a relative reduction in word error rate of 33.2% compared to a state of the art method.
items.title: Decaf: A privacy preserving speech codec using speaker disentanglement and canonical voice conversion

items.summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

items.summary: Every element of the causal chain that produced the five largest mass extinctions of the last half-billion years is presently accelerating in the Earth system. The rate of the modern perturbation exceeds every peer-reviewed paleoclimate reference case. A six-intervention portfolio, deployed together at wartime industrial scale beginning now, is the physically necessary and sufficient response. The window in which that portfolio remains fully effective closes between 2028 and 2040. The anthropogenic-versus-feedback tipping point is expected between 2035 and 2040; corrected for the at-least-order-of-magnitude higher rate of contemporary carbon release, loss of agency — the point at which coordinated intervention can no longer arrest the cascade — arrives 200 to 400 years after feedback engagement under sustained portfolio deployment, and collapses onto the tipping point itself under any scenario in which the portfolio is not deployed within the 2028–2040 window. Background. The five largest mass-extinction events of the Phanerozoic share a consistent causal chain: rapid carbon injection to the ocean-atmosphere system, followed by warming, ocean deoxygenation, acidification, and preferential loss of marine calcifiers, with multi-million-year recovery for reef ecosystems. Every element of that chain is presently active and gaining speed. The current anthropogenic perturbation is capable of driving a combination and magnitude of ocean geochemical changes unparalleled in the geological record reviewed by Hönisch et al. (2012), which covers approximately the past 300 million years. The reef–ocean-oxygen–land coupling documented in the End-Permian record demonstrates that marine biosphere collapse propagates to terrestrial extinction through the shared oxygen and biogeochemical infrastructure of the coupled Earth system; contemporary marine indicators are therefore leading indicators of terrestrial as well as marine risk. Approach. This three-part synthesis compiles peer-reviewed reconstructions of the Big Five causal chain, measures each element against the contemporary Earth system using the most recent authoritative data (Friedlingstein et al. 2026; Wu et al. 2021; Zeebe et al. 2016; Hönisch et al. 2012; Schmidtko et al. 2017; Eddy et al. 2021; Spady et al. 2026), specifies the physically necessary intervention portfolio, and characterizes the near-term feedback, resource, and civilizational risk environment those interventions must succeed in. Part I establishes the paleoclimate analog. Part II specifies the intervention portfolio. Part III maps the contemporary Earth system the Part II portfolio must succeed in — which climate feedbacks are already engaged and how they cascade, which physical resources are hitting hard limits inside the same two-to-three-decade window, and how those pressures translate into food, water, migration, health, economic, and governance strain — and closes with the North American Climate Pain Scale (NAPS), a 1–10 diagnostic instrument that anchors climate severity to concrete events so policymakers and the public can locate today's conditions and the trajectory ahead. Findings. Every element of the paleoclimate extinction causal chain is presently active. Atmospheric CO₂ (422.8 ppm, 2024 global annual mean; Friedlingstein et al. 2026) has exceeded the reconstructed latest-Permian baseline of 426 (+133 / −96) ppm (Wu et al. 2021, Nature Communications). The rate of contemporary carbon release is at least an order of magnitude above the sustained maximum Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum rate (Zeebe, Ridgwell and Zachos 2016, Nature Geoscience). Ocean acidification is proceeding at roughly ten times the PETM rate (Hönisch et al. 2012, Science). The global ocean has lost 4.8 ± 2.1 petamoles of dissolved oxygen since 1960 (Schmidtko, Stramma and Visbeck 2017, Nature). Global living coral cover has declined approximately 50 percent since 1957 (Eddy et al. 2021, One Earth), with cumulative satellite reef-

items.summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
items.title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

We show that DECAF operating at a bit rate of 0.5 kbps achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of up to 43.5% for a speaker verification system, while maintaining competitive ASR performance, yielding a relative reduction in word error rate of 33.2% compared to a state of the art method.
items.title: Decaf: A privacy preserving speech codec using speaker disentanglement and canonical voice conversion

items.summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies Marco Mantovanelli's A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws. It contains the manuscript PDF, complete LaTeX source, six vector figures, independent verification programs, figure-generation code, numerical reports, and sampled figure data. The paper studies Q(n) = Q(n - Q(n-1)) + Q(n - Q(n-2)) - (-1)^n for n >= 8, with the seven prescribed initial values (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5). A causal binary-word construction proves global existence and an exact factorization into three signed excursions. Their uniformly convergent Gaussian profiles explain three limiting sign transitions per standard dyadic block and a sharp normalized error envelope of approximately 0.067088003576. The paper also proves exact finite transition locations, an ordered frequency factorization, a shifted 2-adic valuation law on pure dyadic value blocks, and a summatory asymptotic with an explicit continuous periodic term. The archived verification compares all 33,554,432 directly computed terms with an independent word reconstruction, checks complete frequency blocks through level 21, and verifies the exact summatory identity at every even cutoff from 8 through 33,554,432. Separate programs audit the word maps, finite transitions, and exact two-head identities. These computations supplement the general proofs in the manuscript. The original perturbation, OEIS A394051, is discussed for comparison.
items.title: A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws (Reproducibility Archive)

items.summary: The spoof speech detection (SSD) is the essential countermeasure for automatic speaker verification systems. Although SSD with magnitude features in the frequency domain has shown promising results, the phase information also can be important to capture the artefacts of certain types of spoofing attacks. Thus, both magnitude and phase features must be considered to ensure the generalization ability to diverse types of spoofing attacks. In this paper, we investigate the failure reason of feature-level fusion of the previous works through the entropy analysis from which we found that the randomness difference between magnitude and phase features is large, which can interrupt the feature-level fusion via backend neural network; thus, we propose a phase network to reduce that difference. Our SSD system: phase network equipped Res2Net achieved significant performance improvement, specifically in the spoofing attack for which the phase information is considered to be important. Also, we demonstrate our SSD system in both known- and unknown-kind SSD scenarios for practical applications.
items.title: Phase-Aware Spoof Speech Detection Based on Res2Net with Phase Network

items.title: A reverse reaction can create attracting oscillations

items.summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
items.title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

items.summary: Climate change affects human well-being through interacting physical, ecological, infrastructural, and socioeconomic processes rather than through a single exposure or disease pathway. Major assessments identify observed harms to health, food and water security, livelihoods, settlements, and ecosystems, alongside increasing risks with additional warming (IPCC, 2022a). This narrative review develops a cross-sector framework from a source inventory of 154 human-impact pathways in 14 domains, supported by major assessments, selected peer-reviewed studies, and institutional datasets. Literature selection used targeted web-index searches and source verification through 2 October 2026; the review does not estimate pooled effects or claim exhaustive systematic coverage. The synthesis distinguishes direct injury and illness, ecosystem-mediated harms, failures of essential services, financial transmission, and losses of social and cultural continuity. Representative quantitative findings illustrate substantial existing burdens, but attribution studies, ecological associations, exposure models, displacement records, and conditional forecasts measure different quantities and cannot be combined into a universal five-year trajectory (Vicedo-Cabrera et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2026; Clement et al., 2021). Compound hazards and service interdependencies can increase losses beyond the directly affected sector, while repeated shocks can reduce the capacity to recover or adapt (Zscheischler et al., 2018; IPCC, 2023). A reporting framework is proposed that records the outcome, population, baseline, geography, time horizon, emissions and development assumptions, adaptation, and uncertainty for each indicator. The central contribution is an integrated interpretation and measurement architecture, not a new forecast of global mortality, migration, or societal collapse. Effective assessment should preserve evidence of serious and interacting harms without converting uncertain thresholds or heterogeneous studies into unsupported calendar-specific predictions.
items.title: Climate change impacts humans: A cross-sector narrative review of impact pathways, cascading risks, and accountable quantification

items.summary: Coding agents can now interpret a specification, implement it, write and execute tests, repair failures, and declare the result ready for release. When the same agentic system produces both the software and the evidence of its correctness, a passing test suite no longer constitutes independent evidence. Visible tests become an optimization target, and code, tests, and oracles may share a single misinterpretation of the specification. This paper argues that agent-produced software requires an assurance plane that is structurally independent of the build plane. We first characterize four gaps along the chain from stakeholder intent to production, namely the requirement, conformance, evaluation, and model gaps, and identify which of them verification can close. We then propose a framework that separates building from verifying, introduces a Verification Contract stating what must be demonstrated before release, and organizes verification in two phases: a specification-first phase designed without access to the implementation, and an implementation-aware phase that strengthens the evidence through mutation analysis, property-based testing, and fuzzing. The resulting evidence is consolidated into an assurance report that makes residual uncertainty explicit and leaves the release decision to a human. We evaluate the framework in a pre-registered study on three stateful services, two of them written by third-party models, and an EvalPlus pilot, comparing self-validation with independent verification under context-level and model-level independence. The builder's programs were correct, but its own tests missed subtle interactions: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006), and surfaced the ambiguities of the specification, at the price of rare false oracles. A verifier from another provider did not add detection. The framework and the study provide a basis for governing the release of software produced by agents.
items.title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software

items.summary: Audio deepfakes generated by neural text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems threaten speaker verification and public discourse at scale. The core challenge is cross-dataset generalization: detectors trained on one synthesis pipeline collapse on unseen forgeries. We argue that this failure is primarily because of structural synthetic speech artifacts which are multi-timescale trajectory anomalies. Though every existing detector aggregates a fixed-window frame statistics, this misaligns the architecture with the signal. We propose FlowFake, a Liquid Time-Constant (LTC) architecture whose hidden state evolves via a learned ODE, with per-neuron adaptive time constants simultaneously resolving spectral (10ms) and prosodic (2s) cues. At only 34K parameters FlowFake achieves formal BIBO stability and O(dt^4) integration error. On a four-dataset cross domain benchmark (ASVspoof2019-LA, FakeOrReal, InTheWild, MLAAD), FlowFake reaches 75.29% on ASVspoof2019 trained only on FakeOrReal and 79.97% trained only on MLAAD. It outperforms RawGAT-ST and Whisper-DF on every evaluated pair and matching SSL Wav2vec2 (300x larger) at 0.01% of its parameter count. The source code is available on : https://github.com/GhostRider2023/FlowFake
items.title: FlowFake: Liquid Networks for Audio Deepfake Detection

items.summary: C. J Tully. Independent Research https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   18 th October 2026                   Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late. Something happens. A sound, a face, a tightness in the chest. Before you have chosen anything, a voice — yours, apparently — has already named it, judged it, and filed it under a chapter called me. You do not notice the filing. You notice the file. And so you spend your days inside a commentary about a world you have not, strictly speaking, met. This is not a moral failure. It is a timing error. Awareness is not a mood you work up and not a belief you adopt. It is what is already underway before the sentence starts. The breath you are taking does not consult your biography. The light on the wall does not ask what you meant to become. For a fraction of a second there is contact without a commentator. Then the commentator returns, a little late, a little proud, and explains what just occurred as if the explanation were the event. People talk about waking up as if it were a prize for the patient and the pure. It is closer to catching a clerical mistake. You have been treating the report as the room. The report is useful. It gets you across streets, through grief, into love, out of traffic. It is also not the thing it reports on. The word water has never once made a hand wet. Watch the exact moment a thought claims you. There is a sensation, then a grab. The grab feels like identity. It is older than that, and thinner. It is a habit of ownership so practiced it forgot it was optional. You do not have to defeat it. You only have to notice that noticing is already happening, and that the one who seems to be doing the noticing cannot be found as an object inside what is noticed. Sit with that past the point of comfort. Comfort is how the narration gets rehired. If the “you” who plans, defends, remembers, and suffers is a pattern appearing in awareness, then who has been afraid all this time? Not a cosmic answer. A local one. Look. Fear is weather. The sky it crosses was not manufactured by the storm. Nothing theatrical follows from this. You will still want things. You will still lose them. You will still answer the message and miss the person. The only change is a small, stubborn order of operations: experience first, story second. And the recognition, quiet enough to miss if you perform it, that you were never inside the story. You were the place it was being told. That place does not improve. It does not arrive. It does not need you to become someone else in order to be what it already is. The only work, if it can even be called work, is to stop leaving a half-second early — to remain, once, with what is here before you agree with your own explanation of it. Stay. The explanation can wait. It always could.
items.title: Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late.

items.summary: Singing Accompaniment Generation (SAG) is the process of generating instrumental music for a given clean vocal input. However, existing SAG techniques use source-separated vocals as input and overfit to separation artifacts. This creates a critical train-test mismatch, leading to failure on clean, real-world vocal inputs. We introduce AnyAccomp, a framework that resolves this by decoupling accompaniment generation from source-dependent artifacts. AnyAccomp first employs a quantized melodic bottleneck, using a chromagram and a VQ-VAE to extract a discrete and timbre-invariant representation of the core melody. A subsequent flow-matching model then generates the accompaniment conditioned on these robust codes. Experiments show AnyAccomp achieves competitive performance on separated-vocal benchmarks while significantly outperforming baselines on generalization test sets of clean studio vocals and, notably, solo instrumental tracks. This demonstrates a qualitative leap in generalization, enabling robust accompaniment for instruments - a task where existing models completely fail - and paving the way for more versatile music co-creation tools. Demo audio and code: https://anyaccomp.github.io
items.title: AnyAccomp: Generalizable Accompaniment Generation via Quantized Melodic Bottleneck

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.
items.title: Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc

items.summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
items.title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
items.title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

items.summary: Data and analytical software for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete This repository accompanies the article “Analytical modelling of thermally activated iron-based shape memory alloy fibre concrete: Finite transfer and capacity compatibility”. It provides the numerical source data, analytical implementation, calibration inputs, and results used to prepare the final article. The work examines finite fibre–matrix transfer, thermally activated composite response, cohesive-law identification, and the compatibility of reported strengths with uncertain fibre orientation and tensile capacity. The deposit contains one final analysis snapshot. It includes the reference formulation and the baselines, thermal alternatives, and cohesive-law candidates examined in the article. These are parts of the reported scientific assessment, rather than separate manuscript versions. Superseded model results, development archives, manuscript drafts, and unrelated source files are excluded. Contents • data/ contains numerical representations of published response curves, reported group statistics, study metadata, fixed constituent and pullout calibrations, optimizer initialization values, and published experimental/finite-element comparison curves. Curve identifiers preserve the link to the source study and figure. These are processed publication-based data, rather than original instrument records. • model/ contains the executable analysis scripts. They fit the concrete and composite controls, evaluate reference responses and competing baselines, compare response curves on matched displacement grids, assess orientation and conditional envelopes, test capacity compatibility, verify the independent finite-transfer solver, and fit/test the nested cohesive laws. model/screen_capacity.py provides a command-line conditional strength screen. • model/fesma/ contains the reusable mechanics: the Fe-SMA backbone and bond-slip law, nonuniform pullout and work-quadrature solvers, concrete/cohesive section response, activation and two-ended bridging diagnostics, capacity-budget relations, analytical envelopes and inverse compatibility relations. Every script and module is described individually in docs/FILE_GUIDE.md, including its inputs and outputs. • results/ contains the final reference results, source calibration/diagnostic outputs, orientation transfer matrices, conditional envelopes and containment checks, inverse compatibility calculations, numerical verification records, and cohesive-law fitting/exclusion results. The candidate fit files and specimen-exclusion folds document the model comparisons reported in the article. • figures/ contains the final analytical/numerical TikZ figure sources and the exact numerical series plotted in them. The figure index links these files to the article numbering. Source experimental photographs are excluded. The supplied figure data preserve the published snapshot; numerical reruns write to results/. • docs/ contains the full file guide, source bibliography, data dictionary, equation-to-code crosswalk, figure/plot-series indices, screening instructions and reproduction-check record. FILE_INDEX.csv provides a searchable inventory of every deposited file and its purpose. Individual analysis scripts • model/fit_concrete.py — Fits 20 source-coordinate concrete compression envelopes and evaluates matrix thermal-retention candidates. • model/reproduce_source_diagnostics.py — Recalculates the source-specific thermal and matched-rate baselines, finite recovery sensitivity, and six two-ended bridging scenarios used in Figures 6, 8 and 9. • model/fit_reference.py — Refits the two PD matrix controls and nine fibre-control groups; derives PF matrix inputs, calibrates the DT activation index, and computes reference strengths and sensitivity profiles. • model/check_reference.py — Checks section refinement, force balance and capac
items.title: Data and analytical models for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete: Finite transfer, cohesive response and capacity compatibility

items.summary: Replication files for “Bans versus Controlled Access: Reserve Substitution and Issuer Buybacks under Financial Sanctions”. The A7A5 archive covers the TRON base contract TLeVfrdym8RoJreJ23dAGyfJDygRtiWKBZ from 7–27 August 2025 UTC. Data were retrieved on 17 October 2026 UTC. It includes 5,244 unique events from 37 daily response pages, additional event-class and receipt checks, frozen source responses and request provenance, event-level records, daily and weekly aggregates, supply accounting, data definitions, and analysis and verification scripts. Coverage is specific to the queried contract and provider. Gross transfers do not measure trading volume, beneficial ownership, reserve flows, or issuer buyback expenditure. The pilot is descriptive and does not identify a causal sanctions effect. The model archive contains Python scripts and supplied outputs for hypothetical numerical examples of route substitution, constrained issuer purchases, monitoring-dependent depth, surplus access and fallback. Parameters are not calibrated to A7A5. Both archives use Python 3.9 or later and its standard library; their README files give offline reproduction commands. Access: metadata are public; files are restricted and available on request to the corresponding author, hyoungkang@hanyang.ac.kr. The accompanying RIGHTS_AND_SOURCES.md distinguishes author-created materials from third-party responses. Rights in original materials are reserved; no blanket open license is granted for the mixed archive. The associated manuscript is unpublished.
items.title: A7A5 pilot data and model replication files for Bans versus Controlled Access

items.summary: Embedding enhancement improves speaker verification under acoustic mismatch without modifying a frozen backbone. Recent work has established a practical label-free setting for this task, but often adopts increasingly structured formulations. Here, the clean target is directly observed during training, making enhancement a matching problem on the unit hypersphere. We model the clean target with a von Mises--Fisher (vMF) likelihood and profile out a sample-wise concentration parameter, yielding a simple closed-form objective with adaptive weighting. Across VoxCeleb1, VoxSRC23, CN-Celeb, VOiCES, and VC-Mix, the proposed method largely preserves the baseline and gives clearer gains on challenging mismatch sets. It also remains stable under a broad single-view recipe, where a recent diffusion baseline becomes less reliable in controlled comparisons. These results suggest that effective label-free embedding enhancement in this setting does not require a highly structured formulation.
items.title: Revisiting Label-Free Speaker Embedding Enhancement with vMF Profile Likelihood

items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. Author: Lisa Doumbouya   Research programme: Harmonic Physics Research Programme keywords: String theory; Sine-Gordon equation; Pohlmeyer reduction; Classical strings; Phase dynamics; Coupled phase fields; Relative phase; Cosine interaction; Breather solutions; Solitons; Nonlinear dynamics; Expansion and contraction; Computational reproducibility; Phase theory; Harmonic Physics
items.title: String Theory and Phase Dynamics: An Exact Conditional Sine-Gordon Correspondence

items.summary: Large language models often penalize multilingual users through hidden 'tokenizer taxes' caused by subword fragmentation. Geographic proper nouns offer a controlled stress case for this distributional asymmetry, as they are standardized, cross-linguistically available entities whose orthographic forms frequently mismatch tokenizer training distributions. We introduce the Cross-Linguistic Orthographic Uniqueness Score (CLOUS), a character-level metric based on Shannon surprisal that quantifies the orthographic rarity of localized country names. We evaluate CLOUS on a controlled corpus of 249 ISO-registered country names; generalization to other geographic entity types remains future work. We evaluate CLOUS against tokenization fertility for six production tokenizers spanning three algorithm families across eleven languages and seven script families. Using Spearman rank correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, CLOUS shows significant associative strength with fertility in 61 of 65 valid language-tokenizer combinations. As a screening tool for high-fragmentation entities, CLOUS achieves ROC-AUC = 0.850 and F1 = 0.740, correctly identifying approximately three-quarters of the highest-fragmentation entities from orthographic properties alone. We further show that CLOUS correlates with fertility more strongly than length-based baselines across all evaluated scripts, and outperforms a character bigram surprisal model in 69.2% of tested combinations, particularly for logographic, syllabic, and Latin scripts. Conversely, the bigram baseline proves superior for morphophonologically complex scripts like Arabic and Devanagari, indicating that tokenizer fragmentation is driven by local orthographic context in some scripts and absolute character rarity in others. Script family appears to be the primary driver of CLOUS-fertility correlation strength, with effect sizes ranging from modest for Latin-script languages ) to large for non-Latin scripts (   up to 0.686 for Japanese). These findings suggest that CLOUS may be useful as a lightweight pre-tokenization diagnostic for multilingual NLP pipelines.
items.title: Estimating Cross-Lingual Tokenization Fragmentation Risk: A Frequency-Based Uniqueness Score for Geographic Entities

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.
items.title: Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc

items.summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.
items.title: Resilient Decentralized Shape Formation of Multi-Robot Swarms Under Adversarial Real-World Faults in High-Complexity Disaster Environments

items.summary: Language-queried audio source separation (LASS) enables extracting any sound source using natural language. However, adapting LASS models to application-specific sound classes is challenging due to noisy training data and limited semantic coverage of the CLAP-based control signals. We propose a framework comprised of an automated data engine for training-data curation and a two-stage optimization process for class-specific CLAP control signals. Our objective evaluations across seven sound classes show that data refinement and control signal optimization consistently improve source separation performance. Subjective evaluation with 17 participants further demonstrates perceptual improvements of the model trained with optimized control signals over baseline and similar commercial models.
items.title: A Study on Improving Multi-class Audio Source Separation Via Decoupled CLAP Query Optimization and an Automated Data Engine
